thread:
Anna Chen: quick check-in on the idea I mentioned in the RFC followup: a tiered-SLO backpressure ladder that degrades features predictably rather than flipping to fallbacks abruptly
Devon Li: sounds useful. can you sketch the degradation steps?
Anna Chen: goal is deterministic user-visible behavior per tenant when capacity hits soft limits. ladder = [grace, degrade-quality, degrade-latency, deny] where each step has clear cost/latency tradeoffs
Ravi Patel: how is this different than our current preemptive slots + fallback model?
Anna Chen: current model is binary per-request (allowed vs fallback). ladder gives intermediate modes: e.g. 1) allow with small token-bucket delay; 2) route to cheaper quantized variant; 3) favor shorter sequences + prefix caching; 4) reject with 429. we tie steps to tenant tier and regional capacity
Marta Gomez: important: we need observability hooks per-step and rollout gates. otherwise ops can't tell if "degrade-quality" is harming output quality
Anna Chen: agreed. plan: emit events: degradation_entered, degradation_exited, degradation_reason, active_variant. expose per-tenant counters and sample outputs for evals
Devon Li: what triggers transitions? static thresholds, adaptive signals, or explicit controller?
Anna Chen: hybrid. base policy via SLO windows (p95 latency + available GPUs). then adjust with short-term backpressure signal from serving nodes (queue depth, kv-cache pressure). controller runs on policy engine and issues step transitions per tenant-region pair
Ravi Patel: risk: oscillation between degrade/allow. need hysteresis + min dwell time
Anna Chen: yes, propose: min_dwell=60s, cool_down multiplier if we oscillate more than 3 times in 10m. also use exponentially weighted moving avg for queue depth
Marta Gomez: API surface: do we surface step as part of request trace? e.g., header X-Redwood-Degrade: degrade-quality
Devon Li: header + per-request metric tags. also add fallback_reason to traces so evals can correlate output drift
Anna Chen: sample config snippet for policy engine:
```
policy: {
  slo_window: 5m,
  p95_limit_ms: 120,
  ladder: [grace, degrade-quality, degrade-latency, deny],
  triggers: {
    grace: {queue_depth_lt: 50},
    "degrade-quality": {gpu_util_gt: 0.85, cost_signal_gt: 0.3},
    "degrade-latency": {queue_depth_gt: 200},
    deny: {region_exhausted: true}
  },
  min_dwell_s: 60,
  oscillation_threshold: {count:3, window:600}
}
```
Ravi Patel: how do cost signals fit? we already have per-tenant budgeting and region pricing. want to avoid thrashing tiny tenants on cost spikes
Anna Chen: cost_signal is smoothed and weighted by tenant budget priority. small tenants get earlier degrade-quality vs deny. enterprise tenants have higher grace credits
Marta Gomez: testing plan? need canary + simulation harness that replays traffic mixes and model variants
Devon Li: we should add a "opacity" mode for 24-48h where policy only emits decisions to telemetry but doesn't enforce, so ops and ML can validate quality impact
Anna Chen: good call. routing-bot: will create canary job and surfacing dashboards for ladder states
routing-bot: created job redwood/routing/ladders/canary-170750 with sample tenants and 1h run. canary link: https://internal.redwood/canaries/170750
Ravi Patel: ok. next steps: I can wire eviction/hysteresis code in the runtime adapter if you add the policy flags. Anna, can you file the followup RFC with config knobs and observability contract?
Anna Chen: filing now — will include telemetry schema, sample dashboards, and the simulated workloads. thanks all. :thumbsup:
